messages:
Alex: Quick question — PR #4211 touches multiple dirs (infra, runtime, docs). CODEOWNERS lists /infra -> infra-team, /runtime -> runtime-team, docs has no owner. Release window is tomorrow morning. Who can give a merge approval or proxy? I'm happy to create a temporary CODEOWNERS exception if someone signs off.

Jordan: Which files exactly? small change or broader?

Alex: Files:
```
M docs/README.md
M infra/k8s/alerting.yaml
M runtime/handler/main.go
```
The runtime change is minor (rename var + test updates), infra is a pod annotation tweak, docs is a one-liner. Tests pass locally.

Rachel: I can approve the runtime part if CI is green. @Sam can you take infra? :+1:

Sam: I can take infra. Quick check — does alerting change affect prod alerts? If not, I can approve now.

Alex: No behavioral change, just add `team: infra-alerts` annotation to the pod to route alerts. Not changing thresholds.

Sam: OK I'll review and approve after CI.

Emily: For docs, no owner — anyone on eng-docs ok to approve? If it's purely README wording, I'll sign off.

Jordan: Do we need two approvals per CODEOWNERS? I thought runtime needs one owner + one reviewer.

Rachel: For that path, repo requires 1 owner approval. QA already ran. Should be fine.

merge-bot: PR #4211 status: CI passed on branch 'release/2026.03'. Merge blocked: awaiting required approvals.

Alex: Great — tagging: @Rachel @Sam @Emily. If all three approve, can someone click merge? I won't be on pager during release window.

Sam: Approved 👍

Rachel: Approved ✅

Emily: Approved — docs ok from me.

merge-bot: PR #4211 status: All required approvals received. Merge scheduled in 5m unless blocked.

Alex: Thanks everyone! Leaving a note for audit: temporary proxy approvals from Rachel/Sam/Emily for mixed-codeowners PR.

Jordan: Noted. I'll add a short line in the release notes about the annotation change.

Alex: Perfect.
